8.2 ENERGY ALTERNATIVES
Alternatives to the proposed action, including alternative types of generation, the purchase of power, electric energy conservation measures, and revision of rate structures, have been considered. The state of the art of the so-called exotic sources of electric power such as solar, wind, fusion, magnetohydrodynamic, and fly-wheel energy storage power is such that none of these are, at this time, viable alternatives to the proposed action. Other power sources which are reasonable are: (1) nuclear power, (2) fossil steam, (3) simple cycle combustion turbines, (4) combined cycle combustion turbines, (5) conventional hydroelectric power, and (6) pumped storage hydroelectric power. Additional alternatives to the proposed action are electric energy conservation, modification of rate structures, purchase of power, and denial of the application for license.
8.2.1 Conventional Hydroelectric Power
The convential hydroelectric project is an ideal source of peaking power generating capacity, when available. It affords very rapid response to changes in load and to emergency demands. The forced outage rate of such plants is very low, making their reliability very high. They consume no fuel and produce no combustion products to pollute the air or water.
FPC Staff Study has revealed no site which could be developed to produce peaking capacity equal to that of the proposed Bad Creek Project.
8.2.2 Pumped Storage Hydroelectric Peaking Power
Pumped storage hydroelectric peaking plants such as the proposed Bad Creek Project have most of the engineering advantages of conventional hydro plants. They are capable of very rapid response to changes in load and to emergency demands for their full output capacity in the event of major system faults. From the viewpoint of quickly providing large blocks of emergency relief generating capacity which may be required when major system faults or outages occur, the pumped storage plant has, under certain conditions, an advantage which is common to no other presently available form of generating capacity.
